title: Luther L. Allin, Jr., et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: Three specifications were sustained: inadequate ten-day notice, Wallace Bristow’s improper participation, and Pastor Vitullo’s improper participation and vote. The claim that Presbytery mandated officer rotation was denied. The complaint was remanded for a properly noticed hearing and appropriate action.
first_summary: Session members challenged Presbytery’s order for a congregational meeting on officer rotation and its handling of the complaint hearing. The Judicial Commission sustained objections to inadequate notice and participation by Bristow and Pastor Vitullo, but held that Presbytery had not mandated rotation. It remanded for a properly noticed hearing.
summary: Session members challenged Presbytery’s order to hold a congregational meeting on officer rotation and its handling of the complaint hearing. The Judicial Commission held that ten days ran from the notice’s postmark and that Bristow and Pastor Vitullo could not participate as members of the reviewing court. It nevertheless upheld Presbytery’s authority to require the meeting: a sufficient petition left the Session no option to refuse, while the congregation retained authority to decide rotation. The complaint was sustained in part and remanded for a properly noticed hearing.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The heading identifies the parties (line 1); the Assembly approved and admitted the Judicial Commission’s report to record (lines 158–168, printed p. 105).
evidence_notes.dispute: The four issues concerned ten-day notice, participation by Bristow and Vitullo, and whether Presbytery mandated rotation (lines 188–195, printed p. 105).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Notice was measured from the postmark; participation was improper; a one-fourth petition required a meeting but left rotation to the congregation (lines 197–227). The judgment sustained three specifications, denied one, and remanded (lines 229–241, printed p. 106).
evidence_notes.qualifications: All members concurred; the Commission noted that its appellate limitations prevented consideration of some observed improprieties (lines 243–254, printed p. 106).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference.
